claims.statement: An RGB image has red, green, and blue channel values at each pixel; in this CHW convention, [3,16,16] means one image with three channels, and the three channel planes describe the same spatial coordinates.

evidence.supports: R/G/B are red/green/blue bands and each pixel has one value per band.
Official image conversion puts HWC into CHW.
Tensor shape and indexing describe multidimensional grouped data, with no inherent image/batch meaning.

claims.scope: The semantic interpretation follows this project RGB input convention; the first axis is not universally a color or batch axis. Displaying planes separately is possible but does not turn them into the original combined RGB image.

claims.statement: The exact scene("red","square") fence prints shape(3,16,16), center[1,0,0], top-left[0,0,0], and batch shape(1,3,16,16); changing only red to blue yields center[0,0,1] with the same shapes and black background.
claims.location: 10.1 Python fence, following expected output, final prescribed exercise; introduction 16x16 red-square starting point

evidence.supports: Defaults, fixed color dictionary, zeros background and deterministic square mask yield the printed values.
The center falls inside the square and upper-left outside.

claims.scope: Only the default16x16 square with offset0 and the prescribed red-to-blue change; these deterministic pixels provide no trained recognition evidence.

verification.observed: Both exact programs produced every stated value; supplemental assertions passed.
verification.details: Executed the literal lesson fence and the literal fence with only scene red changed to blue against the inspected current module on CPU.
verification.tolerance: Exact equality: scene uses representable0.0 and1.0 and integer shapes.

claims.statement: tuple(image.shape) reads the axis lengths, and image[:,8,8].tolist() returns the pixel values as a Python list; these display conversions do not change the original image values, shape, or axis order.

evidence.supports: Size is a tuple subclass; shape aliases size; tolist returns Python nested lists or a scalar number.

claims.scope: For the displayed non-scalar RGB slice, tolist returns a one-level list. GPU-to-CPU conversion and nondifferentiability are outside this CPU display example.

verification.expected: Read(3,16,16) and RGB list; original tensor remains equal to its clone with unchanged shape.
verification.observed: Shape/pixel printing matches; modifying the returned Python list leaves image unchanged.
verification.details: Compared the tensor against a clone before and after tuple/toList conversion and mutation of the resulting Python list.

claims.statement: The colon in image[:,8,8] retains all channels while the two integer indices select the same zero-based spatial coordinate; image_batch[0] selects the first full image and image_batch[0,:,8,8] its center RGB.
claims.location: 10.1 explanation after fence and paragraph6 batch indexing

evidence.supports: Full slicing keeps its axis and integer indexing selects/removes the current axis.

evidence.locator: applySlicing lines222-254 and getter dispatch lines391-459
evidence.supports: Python tuple indices are visited in order and passed to the tensor indexing implementation.

claims.scope: Axes refer to the documented CHW and BCHW arrangements. Index8 selects the project-designated center coordinate; it is not an assertion of one unique geometric center on an even-sized grid.

verification.observed: All expected indices passed; asymmetric(3,2,4) diagnostic[:,1,2]=[6,14,22].
verification.details: Verified same-coordinate channel selection with a deliberately asymmetric diagnostic and a red/blue two-image batch; independently ran prerequisite axis examples.

claims.statement: unsqueeze(0) inserts one leading length1 axis so this image has batch shape(1,3,16,16), without adding pixels or changing colors; combining two images gives leading batch length2.

evidence.supports: It inserts a size-one dimension at the specified position and shares underlying data.

evidence.locator: Tensor Views opening and view-operation list
evidence.supports: unsqueeze is a view; creating the view changes data interpretation, not pixel storage.

claims.scope: The leading axis is called a batch axis by the image-interface convention. A returned view aliases the source, so later in-place writes through it could change the source; the lesson claims only that calling this operation does not alter pixels.

verification.expected: Inserted shape(1,3,16,16), unchanged source shape(3,16,16), same768 values; two-image batch(2,3,16,16).
verification.observed: All shape/value assertions passed; unsqueezed data_ptr equals image data_ptr; both batch centers are correct.
verification.details: Compared shape, numel, storage pointer, equality, and torch.stack of the red and blue images.

claims.statement: An HWC image layout must be converted to the axis order the model expects; reinterpreting or reshaping the same numbers as CHW can attach values to the wrong coordinates or channels.
claims.location: 10.1 paragraph4 last sentence and paragraph5 input-convention warning

evidence.supports: The official conversion explicitly transposes/permutates HWC into CHW.
A permutation returns a view with the requested dimension ordering.
Tensor values are stored with a multidimensional strided interpretation.

claims.scope: This is a layout contract, not a universal single layout for every reader/model. A model requires the convention used for its training/input interface; no numerical accuracy penalty is asserted.

claims.statement: Eight-bit RGB photos commonly store channel values0..255; floating conversion and division by255 produces0..1, while this scene already supplies0..1 and should not be divided again. Input range and channel convention must match the model interface.

evidence.supports: RGB is three8-bit bands;8-bit values have range0..255, with other modes/depths listed separately.
Byte images are converted to floating point and divided by255; non-byte inputs are not universally scaled.
Scene writes0.0/1.0 directly into a float zero tensor.
The scale conversion and effect of repeating it follow directly.

claims.scope: The text says often/can, rather than claiming all image formats/dtypes are8-bit RGB. Components here are encoding values, not a claim of linear physical luminance or learned semantic understanding.

sources.title: PyTorch 2.14.1 Tensor size/shape/tolist API docstrings
sources.authority_reason: Original documentation or implementation maintained by the project authors in the official repository.
sources.inspection_note: torch/_tensor_docs.py lines 4737-4777 (size, shape), 5445-5465 (tolist). size returns torch.Size, a tuple subclass; shape aliases size; tolist returns nested Python lists or a scalar number and moves to CPU if necessary.

sources.title: PyTorch 2.14.1 permute/tensor/unsqueeze API docstrings
sources.authority_reason: Original documentation or implementation maintained by the project authors in the official repository.
sources.inspection_note: torch/_torch_docs.py lines 8953-8971 (permute), 9582-9634 (tensor), 12475-12504 (unsqueeze). permute returns a view with dimension order changed; tensor constructs data from Python sequences; unsqueeze inserts a size-one dimension and shares underlying data.

sources.title: PyTorch 2.14.1 C++ TensorIndexing implementation
sources.authority_reason: Original documentation or implementation maintained by the project authors in the official repository.
sources.inspection_note: aten/src/ATen/TensorIndexing.h lines 39-64, 93-111, 202-271, 451-484. A full colon slice defaults start 0, stop maximum; applySlice preserves that dimension and advances dimension cursor; integer selection selects/removes the current dimension. These explain [:,8,8] and batch indices.

sources.title: PyTorch 2.14.1 Python tensor indexing dispatcher
sources.authority_reason: Original documentation or implementation maintained by the project authors in the official repository.
sources.inspection_note: torch/csrc/autograd/python_variable_indexing.cpp lines 222-254, 391-459. Python multidimensional getitem visits the index tuple in order and dispatches each dimension to the C++ indexing implementation.

sources.title: PyTorch 2.14.1 Tensor Views official documentation source
sources.authority_reason: Original documentation or implementation maintained by the project authors in the official repository.
sources.inspection_note: docs/source/tensor_view.md paragraphs Tensor Views, view operations list, indexing note, reshape special behavior. Basic slicing, permute and unsqueeze are view operations sharing data; changing an alias later may mutate the base. Calling the displayed transformations alone leaves original pixel values unchanged.

sources.title: Own deterministic scene, normalization, and prerequisite axis calculations
sources.details: For size=16 and offset=0, center=8 and square half-width=4; indices4..12 contain the square. Thus (8,8) is colored and (0,0) is black; RGB entries follow scene color dictionary. 3*16*16=768 values remain 768 after singleton insertion. For 8-bit values 0<=v<=255, 0<=v/255<=1; already-normalized 1/255 is about0.003921568859368563 in float32. W.3 row sums210,270 divided by3 give70,90; column sums140,160,180 divided by2 give70,80,90; replacing80 by110 gives row mean80 and last-column mean105. Full reasoning and conditions: a-notes.

intro_summary: 章首把圖片輸入界定為數字介面問題：16×16紅方塊的像素需經切塊、特徵與插入位置變成模型可接收的序列。它區分離線合成圖片與10.5已取得的服飾圖，並將介面接通、下一章檢查理解、最後三節比較圖文配對的學習路線連起來。這些說明與先前已核對的scene實作及服飾輸入相符；導言沒有把介面接通當成認圖品質證據，也沒有新增品質或速度數值主張。
